summary: nodes.zip at 22.0.368 holds 5,034 entries = 5,033 .txt + 1 .h; 5,032 are context pages across 19 contexts. The format is NOT consistent across contexts and nine distinct single-parser assumptions were measured false, three of them silent (CRLF, BOM, colon-directive id capture). The join key is the LABEL, confirmed against the live runtime in four separate measurements - it is present on 100% of documented parameter records and resolves 88.7-89.1% of them, against 62-85% presence and 43.4-52.9% resolution for #id. All 161 new Copernicus nodes have a page and 158 clear a stated quality floor. Doc and runtime disagree about deprecation on 195 node types, and 51 of those are the dangerous direction: the runtime flags them while the documentation reads completely clean.

findings.claim: The page format is NOT consistent across contexts. Nine single-parser assumptions were measured false over the full 5,032-page census. The two largest structural splits: cop/ is 98% directives-before-title while lop/ is 79% TITLE-before-directives (897 pages, 17.8%, would yield no #context/#internal from a head-of-file header read); and cop/ puts every parameter at column 0 while cop2/ puts most at indent >=4 (527 pages, 10.5%, would lose EVERY parameter). One parser per context is the correct shape.
findings.severity: blocking for I1 - an extractor written against one assumed structure produces a corpus that looks complete and joins to nothing

findings.claim: THREE SILENT DEFECTS were found in this leg's own reader by its own controls, each returning a plausible number and raising nothing. (D1) splitting on '\n' and anchoring items on '$' returns ZERO parameters on the 138 CRLF/MIXED pages - and 67 of 375 cop/ pages (17.9%) are CRLF, so the defect lands hardest on Copernicus, the exact frontier surface. (D2) decoding 'utf-8' rather than 'utf-8-sig' succeeds on the 58 BOM pages and leaves U+FEFF at offset 0, eating the first directive: 32 pages lose a directive, 26 lose their title. (D3) binding any indented '#id:' to the preceding label re-keys sop/xform's 'Combine' parameter from 'combine' to '406959576' - a Vimeo VIDEO id, because ':vimeo: Transform SOP' blocks carry one.
findings.severity: significant - all three are the 'looks complete, joins to nothing' failure class this leg exists to prevent, and none raises an exception

findings.claim: H9-F1 is CONFIRMED against the live runtime, not inherited: LABEL is the join key. Measured four ways (raw/resolved x hand-picked-15/population-141). method_notes: R60 taken literally: 102 controls across six producers (61+15+4+5+7+10). Each reader carries POSITIVE controls (hand-read pages the parser must reproduce), NEGATIVE controls (a mutation that must drive the count to zero - proving the count measures something) and BLIND-READER controls (a deliberately naive parser shown returning the WRONG answer where ours returns right). The blind readers are kept in the calibration file on purpose as negative instruments.

Law 1 applied to the probes themselves: the Q3 presence test is paired with a fabricated node name that must read ABSENT; the Q2 matcher with a fabricated parm id that must not match; the Q6 detectors with clean text that must yield nothing. Without those, 'all present' and '100% match' are unfalsifiable.

Q1 measures the FULL POPULATION of every context rather than the >=20-per-context sample the brief allows. A census cost the same as a sample at this scale (5,032 pages, ~2s), so the sample size is stated as n = the whole context.

One control FAILED on first run and its EXPECTATION was corrected, not the code: lop/distantlight's raw rung is SUMMARY, not EXISTS, because the page does carry a summary. The claim under test (resolution moves the page across the floor) was unchanged and a second assertion on clears()/clears() was added alongside. One further control was rewritten from an exact count to a liveness assertion because it pinned the arithmetic of a deliberately-broken instrument rather than the control's meaning; the reasoning is recorded inline at the control.

Q2 was measured TWICE - once on raw pages and once with includes resolved - because measuring only raw would have under-sampled exactly the pages where the join is hardest (lop/distantlight is 0 params raw, 87 resolved, and lop is where #id does worst). The verdict is identical in both.

Prior work was reused rather than re-derived where it was committed and calibrated: harness/notes/h9/helpdoc.py supplies the include resolver (four shipped anchor forms, cross-zip path normalisation, cyclic-include guard) and serves as the second instrument for cross-validation. Its own recorded defects informed two of this leg's controls.

No Workflow fan-out was used. R61 records a read-only extraction FLEET that edited five schema files and kept writing after being stopped, in this exact domain; Article I says enforcement belongs in the definition, not the instruction. The single subagent dispatched was of a type whose DEFINITION lacks Edit/Write tools, and it performed prior-art reading only - no measurement.

The archive's own hazards were checked before being assumed: all 5,033 .txt entries decode as strict UTF-8 (an encoding-corruption hypothesis, refuted), but 58 carry a BOM that plain utf-8 decoding silently preserves.

Coincidence flagged so it does not read as a copy error: the Q4 exists-minus-clears gap (202 of 2,141 pages) and the Q6 deprecation union (202 node types) are the same integer by chance. They are unrelated measurements from different producers.

for_ruling.question: H9-F3's '7.7% of cop2 parameter records carry #id; 13 of 139 pages' does not reproduce against nodes.zip at 22.0.368 by any denominator I can construct (measured: 9 of 150 pages, 51 raw #id lines, 4.4% of records), and H9's own final artifact supersedes it at 42.7% once #channels is counted. The stale figure is currently propagated into harness/prompts/i0.md:14 and harness/SYNAPSE_INGEST.md:40 - both of which are deny-listed from agent edit. What should the corrected figure be, and should the brief be amended?
for_ruling.recommendation: Strike the 7.7% / 13-of-139 figures as R86 struck R72's character counts - amended in place, not silently corrected - and replace with the measured pair: 'cop2 carries #id on 4.4% of parameter records, and #channels on a further 248 occurrences; counting both, 42.7% of cop2 parameter records carry an internal name.' H9-F3's CONCLUSION stands and is strengthened: the finding was never really about #id scarcity, it was about cop2 using a DIFFERENT internal-name key. That is the more actionable statement.

for_ruling.question: The two available parsers fail in opposite directions on lop/ - _i0_reader has ~18x the recall at lower precision, helpdoc is precise but under-extracts (12 parameters for a 402-parameter node). I0's coverage numbers carry the high-recall bias. Which bias should I1's corpus adopt, and is a precision pass in scope for I1?
for_ruling.recommendation: High recall with a per-entry confidence field, and a precision pass IN SCOPE for I1: for each extracted parameter, record whether its label resolved against the live runtime at build time. That converts precision from an unknown into a per-entry fact and is consistent with R119 (per-entry provenance, never per-corpus). It also makes the corpus self-auditing on the next build. Cost: one hython pass at corpus-build time.

for_ruling.question: docs/H22_FRONTIER.md's '161' was extracted from the browsing help cache by harness/notes/_h22_frontier_xref.py, which also computes its 'share of all cop pages' denominator from the 25 cached cop pages rather than the 375 shipped ones. news.zip!22/copernicus.txt ships the same page and yields the same 161 exactly. Should the producer be re-pointed at the shipped source?
for_ruling.recommendation: Yes - re-point it at news.zip and fix the denominator to the 375 shipped cop pages. The 161 itself does not change (verified: exact set equality between the two sources), so this is a provenance upgrade rather than a number correction, and it removes a browsing-history dependency from a governing document. Low risk, and it makes the figure reproducible on any machine with the build installed.

for_ruling.question: 51 node types are flagged deprecated by the runtime while their documentation reads completely clean, and they include sop/copy, sop/group, sop/point, sop/paint and both Karma LOPs. R72 rule 3 says the disagreement is itself a finding. Should SYNAPSE surface the runtime axis to artists when the docs are silent, and does the doc-only direction (144, of which 138 are the announced-for-removal cop2 subsystem) warrant the same treatment?
for_ruling.recommendation: Surface both, labelled by source, and never merge them into a single 'deprecated' boolean. The two directions mean different things to an artist: runtime-only means 'the software will stop offering this', doc-only means 'the vendor has announced removal but the build still ships it'. Merging them loses exactly the information an artist needs to plan. This is a product decision about what SYNAPSE says to a user, so it is a ruling item and not an agent call.

for_ruling.question: SPECULATIVE, flagged because it is cheap for a human to check and would otherwise be lost: the shipped documentation contains exactly 385 unresolvable include ANCHORS archive-wide, and H9-F1's unreproducible figure is also 385. I have NO evidence connecting them - my 385 is archive-wide across 19 contexts while H9's scope was lop/cop/cop2, where helpdoc's own stats record 45 unresolved anchors, not 385. On the evidence this is most likely coincidence.
for_ruling.recommendation: Record as a coincidence unless H9's author recognises the number. Do NOT publish the connection - it has no producer and asserting it would be the exact defect I0-F11 reports. Raised only because a reader who notices the collision independently should find it already considered and dismissed rather than missed.

for_ruling.question: This worktree's branch (ingest/i0-ingest-scout at 66752c7) predates the INGEST-01 harness commit (87a5af9 on feat/repair-heats-01), so harness/SYNAPSE_INGEST.md and the I0/I1 entries in harness/legs.json are ABSENT from the leg's own tree. The brief instructed me to read a file the leg cannot see; I read both from the main worktree and recorded it. Should the orchestrator rebase leg worktrees onto the harness commit that defines them?
for_ruling.recommendation: Yes - create leg worktrees from the commit that adds their legs.json entry, or rebase at launch. A leg whose governing document is invisible from its own tree cannot verify its own instructions, and R127 (read committed paths, never worktree globs) assumes the committed path is reachable. Cosmetic this time because the file was readable one directory up and 66752c7 is a clean ancestor of 87a5af9, but it is a silent-drift shape.

what_the_leg_proves_about_its_own_premis: The brief's premise was that 5,034 is a PAGE count and not a KNOWLEDGE count, and that an extractor written against an assumed structure produces a corpus that looks complete and joins to nothing. Both halves are confirmed, and the leg confirmed them on ITSELF before confirming them on the archive: three separate silent defects were found in this leg's own reader by its own controls, and every one returned a plausible number while raising no error. The CRLF defect alone would have scored 67 of 375 Copernicus pages as having zero parameters - on the exact surface docs/H22_FRONTIER.md calls the frontier - and nothing in the output would have looked wrong. The brief also asked me to confirm or refute H9's join-key finding rather than inherit it; doing so confirmed H9-F1 on stronger evidence and REFUTED the numbers in H9-F3 that the brief itself was quoting. A scout that had inherited its brief's premises would have shipped a stale figure into I1's design. That is the case for the leg existing.
